commit.message:
chore: build the plugins against Paseo SDK 0.9.2
Every plugin now pins `@getpaseo/plugin` 0.9.2, and the two that use it `@getpaseo/client` ^0.9.2, matching the Paseo desktop build in use.
The lockfile resolves plugin, client, protocol and relay to 0.9.2.
The published 0.9.2 packages differ from 0.9.1 only in their package.json, so no plugin code changes.
The manifests keep requiring Paseo >=0.9.0, since nothing needs a newer host.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(claude-tty): stop naming the SDK version in CLAUDE.md

It went stale on every bump, while the rule it carries does not depend on the version.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(claude-tty): stop counting the down keys an answered startup menu gets

The tests that expect the adapter to answer the workspace trust, external imports, bypass permissions or stale resume menu named exactly one down key before the confirm.
The adapter looks again 25ms after each key and presses down once more if the marker has not moved, so a runner that stalls past that look before the fake repaints sends two, which failed the workspace trust test on #105's CI.
Those tests now collapse the run of downs before the confirm and assert the rest, and the dropped-key test asserts at least two downs rather than exactly two.
Delaying the fake's repaint by 40ms reproduces the old failure every time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@ -331,7 +331,7 @@ Icons, `Modal`, `useToast` and `copyText` come from `@getpaseo/plugin/client/rea
 
 `pnpm test` is `node --test "{client,server,shared}/**/*.test.ts"` through Node's type stripping, so no TypeScript that has to be emitted and relative imports keep their `.ts` extension.
 A test that resolves the plugin root walks up from `import.meta.dirname`, so it counts the directory it sits in and no `src/` above it.
-`@getpaseo/client` is on 0.9.2 across the workspace, which is what `@getpaseo/plugin` takes as a peer.
+`@getpaseo/client` stays on the version `@getpaseo/plugin` takes as a peer.
 
 `server/acp-provider.test.ts` is the one exception to all of that: it runs the adapter's own `tsc` build and then spawns the result, because the bridge it exercises takes a command rather than a module, and a stale `dist/` would otherwise decide the result.
 It points the adapter at a throwaway state directory so the run touches none of yours.
